research_question.statement: Can drought-resistant maize varieties maintain commercially viable grain yields under managed water-deficit conditions in semi-arid eastern Kenya?

evidence.excerpt: The primary objective was to determine whether these varieties could maintain grain yields above 2.5 tonnes per hectare under managed drought stress.

findings.statement: Variety V2 achieved the highest average grain yield at 3.1 t/ha under drought stress, significantly outperforming V1.

evidence.excerpt: V2 produced a mean yield of 3.1 t/ha (SD = 0.42), which was significantly higher than V1 at 2.3 t/ha (p = 0.008).

findings.statement: V3 yielded 2.8 t/ha under drought stress and was not significantly different from V2, suggesting similar drought tolerance.

evidence.excerpt: V3 yielded 2.8 t/ha (SD = 0.38) and was not significantly different from V2 (p = 0.21).

findings.statement: V2 showed the earliest mean flowering at 68 days after planting compared to 74 days for V1, which may be correlated with drought escape.

evidence.excerpt: V2 showed the earliest mean flowering at 68 days after planting, compared to 74 days for V1.

limitations.statement: The study was conducted at a single site over two seasons, which limits the generalisability of the results to other agro-ecological zones.

evidence.excerpt: The results should be interpreted with caution given that the study was conducted at a single site over two seasons.
